# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: The fix stops the generator and analyzer crashing when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. It changes two diagnostic sites in `TypeCollector` that indexed `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]`. One now uses a new `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` helper and the other uses `FirstOrDefault()`. It also wraps the collector's diagnostic reporter in a filter that silently drops any diagnostic whose location is not a source tree of the current compilation. Three tests compile a defining assembly to an image, reference it as metadata only, and check for no diagnostics and a generated resolver. Two doc sections were added.
story.why: For metadata symbols `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. The generator then emitted nothing, which left the consuming assembly without a resolver.
touches_beyond_requirement: The reporter filter at TypeCollector.cs line 239 applies to every diagnostic the collector reports, not just metadata ones. Any diagnostic created with a null location (Location.None) is now dropped, including for source types.

The cast at line 985 changed from a hard cast to `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. A source property whose syntax is not a property declaration (for example a positional record parameter) now gets a null location, and the filter drops that diagnostic.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md gained new sections. The two disagree with each other, and the MsgPack004 text disagrees with the code.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The crash sites at lines 985 and 1077 and the metadata-only test harness look correct. However, the issue named three crashing sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101) and only two are visibly changed. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path at line 985 is not exercised by any test. The blanket filter changes behaviour for all diagnostics. The MsgPack004 doc describes behaviour the code does not have.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now gets its location through GetPropertyIdentifierLocation. That helper returns null instead of indexing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` when the property has no source declaration. No test exercises this path, because no test uses a null key.
claims.requirement_quote: Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly

breaker.reason: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation on TypeCollector.cs line 1434 did not only replace [0] with FirstOrDefault(); it also replaced the explicit (PropertyDeclarationSyntax) cast with 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax'. Consequently, contrary to the claim and the cited XML comment on line 1433, it also returns null when a property IS declared in source via a record or record struct primary constructor (where GetSyntax() is ParameterSyntax), causing ReportIfLocatedInCompilation to silently drop BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for source positional record properties. Also, from the diff alone one can only verify that the 3 new tests do not use a null key, not the entire test suite.

claims.text: The new README section says closed generic value types from referenced assemblies are supported. It says diagnostics about their members are reported by the defining assembly rather than the consumer. This matches the filter in C2.

breaker.reason: Checked README.md lines 1639-1643: the added section states that closed generic types (including generic value types and record structs) from referenced assemblies can be used as members of MessagePackObject types and that diagnostics on their members are reported by the defining assembly rather than the consuming project, matching C2's filter.

claims.text: The new MsgPack004.md section says members of referenced-assembly types are reported in the consuming project at the using member. The code drops those diagnostics (C2) and test C7 asserts no diagnostic, so this doc statement is not backed by the change.

breaker.reason: Checked doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md lines 48-52 against TypeCollector.cs lines 1077 and 1446: MsgPack004.md claims unattributed public members of referenced-assembly types are reported in the consuming project at the member using the type, whereas TypeCollector creates MemberNeedsKey with a null location for metadata members and ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops it.

claims.text: The collector's reporter is now wrapped so that every diagnostic passes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation before reaching the analyzer callback. When no callback is given it stays null.
claims.requirement_quote: A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

breaker.reason: Checked TypeCollector.cs lines 236-243: reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is only stored in this.reportDiagnostic on line 239, staying null when reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is null and wrapping it in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation otherwise.

claims.text: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in source and its syntax tree belongs to the current compilation. Diagnostics about metadata members, which have a null location, are silently dropped instead of being reported or throwing.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic uses `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?`, so an unkeyed public member of a metadata type no longer throws.

Without knowing whether reportAnalyzerDiagnostic is non-null, the diff alone cannot confirm this test exercises ReportIfLocatedInCompilation ('drop, don't report') rather than this.reportDiagnostic simply being null.

It then runs the generator directly and asserts two things: no Warning-or-higher diagnostics, which would include CS8785, and that the expected resolver hint name is among the generated sources. findings.description: Claim C3 disputed: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation on TypeCollector.cs line 1434 did not only replace [0] with FirstOrDefault(); it also replaced the explicit (PropertyDeclarationSyntax) cast with 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax'. Consequently, contrary to the claim and the cited XML comment on line 1433, it also returns null when a property IS declared in source via a record or record struct primary constructor (where GetSyntax() is ParameterSyntax), causing ReportIfLocatedInCompilation to silently drop BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull for source positional record properties. Also, from the diff alone one can only verify that the 3 new tests do not use a null key, not the entire test suite.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None diagnostics about source types. Previously those were reported, since analyzers may report Location.None. Any existing collector diagnostic whose location helper can return null for a source type would now vanish silently. No test checks that existing source-type diagnostics still fire.

The hard cast changed to `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax`. For a source property whose syntax is not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax (for example a positional record parameter with a null key), the location becomes null and the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic is now silently dropped. This path has no test.

The issue lists three crashing `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101), but the diff changes only two. If a third site remains elsewhere in GetObjectInfo, other metadata generic value types could still crash. Reviewers should grep for remaining `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` usages.

The doc says unattributed public members of referenced-assembly types are flagged in the consuming project. The code drops these diagnostics and ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember asserts none are reported. It also contradicts README line 1642.

For a metadata type with an unkeyed public member, the generator now proceeds silently and generates a formatter in the consuming assembly. The member problem is never surfaced anywhere if the defining assembly did not run the analyzer.

In the ternary branch immediately above line 1077, AOTDerivedKeyAttribute still evaluates derivedKeyAttribute.GetSyntax(this.cancellationToken).GetLocation() unconditionally (even in the generator when reportDiagnostic is null and before line 1078's accessibility check). If a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly has a member annotated with a custom attribute derived from KeyAttribute, the metadata AttributeData has no syntax in source, throwing NullReferenceException and crashing both the generator (CS8785, omitting the resolver) and analyzer (AD0001).

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts GetSyntax() 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', which evaluates to null for positional properties declared in source on a record or record struct primary constructor (whose syntax node is ParameterSyntax). Because ReportIfLocatedInCompilation on line 1446 requires diagnostic.Location.IsInSource, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull is now silently dropped for positional record properties in the current compilation, as is any other diagnostic on a current-compilation type whose location helper returns null (such as GetParameterListLocation on line 1454 when method is null or an implicit constructor).

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (and README.md line 1642) assumes member diagnostics on referenced-assembly types are reported when compiling the defining assembly, but contract assemblies that only reference MessagePack.Annotations without MessagePack.SourceGenerator (or compile without analyzers, as CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync on GenericsFormatterTests.cs line 664 does) never run MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer. Dropping those diagnostics in the consuming project leaves invalid members like unkeyed public properties completely undiagnosed at build time in both projects.
